Implementation Plan

Plan for issue #6276: tie the unblock judge's bulk-delete override to the deletions the guard actually rejected

Planning ref: `git rev-parse HEAD` = `b7c675dbb0afc480dd0dc93069153a54add133ef`, branch `claude/replace-claude-sessions-phase-7`. That matches the integration-branch metadata (mismatch: false). No clarification questions were needed.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends scripts/unblock_ledger.py::validate
Scope-mode justification: The finding is about one control. `validate()` (`scripts/unblock_ledger.py:413-431`) accepts any `override_guard` paths the model picks for `destructive-blocked`. It only filters protected and canonical prefixes, and never checks that the guard rejected those paths. The spend step in `.github/workflows/implement.yml` ("Unblock judge bulk-delete override", lines 1855-1908) then trusts any comment by the pipeline login whose last line is the override marker. Plan and clarify comments are model output posted by that same login, so a comment alone is not provenance. The complete fix has three parts:
- the guard run records what it rejected in a place only that run can write: a workflow artifact;
- the judge accepts only paths that appear in that record;
- the spend step checks the same record again.

All three parts reuse the existing guard handler, ledger validator, judge flow and spend step. The scope-guard override (`scope-blocked`) is a separate surface and stays unchanged. Priorities follow §6: Security, then Correctness & safety.

## Automation / wiring (§20.E)
- No new script. This extends `scripts/implement_handle_guard_block.sh`, `scripts/unblock_ledger.py`, `scripts/unblock_judge.sh` and two steps in `.github/workflows/implement.yml`.
- Entry points:
  - the destructive-guard rejection path in `implement.yml` (step "Handle destructive-commit / scope guard block", which calls `implement_handle_guard_block.sh`);
  - `unblock_judge.yml`, dispatched by the poller's unblock scan, which runs `scripts/unblock_judge.sh`;
  - `implement.yml`, step "Unblock judge bulk-delete override".
- No long-running supervisor. No database work. No entry in `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`.

## 1. Files likely to change
- `scripts/implement_handle_guard_block.sh`: in the destructive branch (after the `case "${DCB_REASON}"` block), write the rejection snapshot JSON and add a pointer marker to the guard comment.
- `.github/workflows/implement.yml`:
  - give the guard-block handler step an `id:` if it has none;
  - add a new upload step right after it;
  - harden the spend step;
  - add `unblock_ledger.py` to the helper staging loop at line 1027.
- `scripts/unblock_ledger.py`:
  - new `rejection-snapshot` subcommand;
  - `validate()` gains a `rejected` argument and a `--rejected-deletions-file` option.
- `scripts/unblock_judge.sh`:
  - when the stop is `destructive-blocked` and the raw verdict is `override_guard`, fetch and verify the snapshot before `validate`;
  - add a `Rejected run: <id>` line to the verdict comment.
- `prompts/mode-judge-unblock.txt`: one rule line saying destructive override paths must be an exact subset of the guard's latest rejected-deletion list.
- Tests:
  - `tests/test_unblock_judge.py`
  - `tests/test_unblock_scan.py`
  - `tests/test_implement_post_codex_recovery.py`
- `agents.md`: the "Unblock judge" bullets that describe `Approved deletions: [...]`.
- `changelog.d/6276-bulk-delete-override-rejection-binding.md`: new changelog fragment.

## 2. Functions / modules to implement
**A. `implement_handle_guard_block.sh` (destructive branch only)**
- Build `${RUNTIME_DIR}/destructive_rejection/destructive_rejection.json` with jq from data the workflow itself produced:
  `{"schema":"destructive_rejection.v1","issue":<ISSUE_NUMBER>,"run_id":<GITHUB_RUN_ID>,"run_attempt":<GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT>,"reason":"<DCB_REASON>","paths":[...]}`
  - `paths` comes from `DCB_DELETIONS`, one per line, empty lines dropped, kept exactly as git printed them.
- Write `rejection_snapshot=true` to `GITHUB_OUTPUT`.
- Append a pointer line to the guard comment: `<!-- ai:destructive-rejection:v1 item=<N> run=<id> attempt=<a> -->`. It is informational only and never used as proof.
- If writing the snapshot fails, warn and carry on. The block itself is unchanged, and no override can be approved later (fail closed).

**B. `implement.yml`, new step "Upload destructive-rejection snapshot"**
- `if: always() && steps.<handler id>.outputs.rejection_snapshot == 'true'`
- `uses: actions/upload-artifact@v6`
- `name: destructive-rejection-issue-${{ env.ISSUE_NUMBER }}`
- `path: ${{ env.RUNTIME_DIR }}/destructive_rejection/destructive_rejection.json`
- `retention-days: 30`, `if-no-files-found: ignore`, `continue-on-error: true`
- The guard step's own `name:`, `if:` and `env:` stay as they are (§10).

**C. `unblock_ledger.py rejection-snapshot`** (pure function, no network)
- Arguments: `--run-file` (run metadata JSON), `--artifact-file` (artifact metadata JSON), `--zip-file`, `--item`, `--repo`, and optionally `--approved-json`.
- Fail closed with `UsageError` unless every check below passes:
  - the run's `repository.full_name` and `head_repository.full_name` both equal `--repo`;
  - `path` is one of the implement workflow files: `.github/workflows/implement.yml`, `internal-implement.yml` or `ai-implement.yml`;
  - `status == completed` and `conclusion == failure`;
  - the artifact is not expired, its `workflow_run.id` equals the run id, and its `size_in_bytes` is at most 1 MiB;
  - the zip contains exactly `destructive_rejection.json`, read with `zipfile` with a size cap;
  - the JSON's `schema`, `issue == item`, `run_id == run.id` and `reason == "bulk-delete"` all match;
  - `paths` is a non-empty list of strings.
- Returns `{"run_id", "reason", "paths"}`.
- With `--approved-json`, it also requires the approved paths to be a subset of `paths`.

**D. `validate(verdict, decision, repo, rejected=None)`**
- Applies only when `name == "override_guard"` and `decision.stop == "destructive-blocked"`.
- If `rejected` is missing or empty, raise `UsageError("override_guard on destructive-blocked needs a verified rejected-deletion snapshot")`.
- Every cleaned path must be in `set(rejected["paths"])`. Otherwise raise `UsageError` naming the first offending path. There is no partial approval.
- Set `normalised["rejected_run"] = rejected["run_id"]`.
- The CLI `validate` command gains an optional `--rejected-deletions-file`.
- The existing canonical, protected and source-repo checks stay unchanged and still run first.

**E. `unblock_judge.sh`, new function `unblock_rejection_snapshot`**
- Runs only when `ITEM_STOP == destructive-blocked`, the item is an issue, and `verdict_raw.json` has `verdict == override_guard`.
- Makes three API calls:
  1. `gh api "repos/${REPOSITORY}/actions/artifacts?name=destructive-rejection-issue-${ITEM}&per_page=5"`, then takes the newest artifact that has not expired;
  2. `gh api "repos/${REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/<run_id>"`;
  3. `gh api "repos/${REPOSITORY}/actions/artifacts/<id>/zip" > snapshot.zip`.
- Runs `unblock_ledger.py rejection-snapshot` and writes the result to `${RUNTIME_DIR}/rejected_deletions.json`.
- Passes `--rejected-deletions-file` to `validate` whenever that file exists.
- Any failure leaves the file absent. `validate` then refuses the verdict and the existing `invalid_verdict` wait path runs, logged as `UNBLOCK_JUDGE ... op=rejection_snapshot outcome=failed reason=<...>`.
- The verdict comment gains a `Rejected run: <id>` line next to `Approved deletions:` (in the jq at line 567).
- §14 audit: none of the existing judge calls (item, comments, check-runs, run log) reads artifacts, so these three calls are new. They run only for this one verdict and stop, and the code gets a comment saying so.

**F. `implement.yml` spend step**
After `approved_deletions` is resolved and before the spend comment is posted:
- Require a `Rejected run: <digits>` line in the override comment. Without it, log `outcome=skip reason=rejection_run_unbound`. This makes old override comments unusable (fail closed).
- Look up the artifact named `destructive-rejection-issue-${ISSUE_NUMBER}` whose `workflow_run.id` equals that run. The artifact must have been created before the override comment's `created_at`.
- Fetch the run and the zip.
- Run `python3 <staged>/unblock_ledger.py rejection-snapshot ... --approved-json "${approved_deletions}"`.
- On any failure, log `outcome=skip reason=rejection_snapshot_unverified` or `reason=approved_paths_not_rejected`, and do not spend the override.
- These calls happen only when an unspent override marker exists. The existing guard (`implement_commit_changes.sh:460` and the inline copy at `implement.yml:3493`) stays unchanged as a third layer: every staged deletion must still be in the approved list.

## 3. Data structures affected
- New artifact `destructive-rejection-issue-<N>` containing `destructive_rejection.v1` JSON. This is a new identifier; it does not collide with existing artifact names.
- The verdict comment body gains a `Rejected run: <id>` line. The marker grammar `<!-- ai:unblock:v1 ... override=bulk_delete -->` is unchanged.
- The guard comment gains the `<!-- ai:destructive-rejection:v1 ... -->` pointer line.
- Normalised verdict JSON gains `rejected_run`. No other field is renamed.

## 4. API / interface changes
- `unblock_ledger.py` gains the `rejection-snapshot` subcommand and the optional `validate --rejected-deletions-file`. Existing commands and outputs are kept.
- New GitHub REST reads: `GET /repos/{r}/actions/artifacts?name=`, `GET /repos/{r}/actions/runs/{id}`, `GET /repos/{r}/actions/artifacts/{id}/zip`. All use the existing `GH_PAT` (repo scope).
- New skip reasons under the existing `UNBLOCK_BULK_DELETE_OVERRIDE` log prefix: `rejection_run_unbound`, `rejection_snapshot_unverified`, `approved_paths_not_rejected`.
